history.dynasty: Rebuilt by Naga sadhus (~16th century, by tradition)
history.period: Legendary origins; present structure ~500 years old (by tradition)
history.summary: An ancient Shiva temple between Hasanganj and Daliganj on the left (eastern) bank of the Gomti. Legend: Lakshman installed the Shivling here after leaving Sita in exile, seeking peace for his troubled mind ('Mann' + 'Kameshwar', fulfiller of desires); King Navdhanu later built a temple with twenty-three golden urns. The temple was destroyed by invaders in the 12th century and rebuilt by Naga sadhus about 500 years ago; it is managed by Mahant Devagya Puri (Arunima Singh), Lucknow's first woman Mahant. Note: some travel listings wrongly place it on the Yamuna at 'Saraswati Ghat' — the temple is on the Gomti at Daliganj. Exact construction dates are traditional, not documented — treat antiquity claims with caution.

name: Mankameshwar Mandir
town_description: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh on the Gomti river, famed for its Nawabi heritage — Awadhi cuisine, chikankari embroidery, the Bara and Chhota Imambaras, and a lively old-city culture of tehzeeb and poetry.

travel.road: Daliganj, on the Gomti riverbank — city buses, autos and cabs
